quickSummary: Inductive (I): σ-polarization (permanent). Resonance (M/R): π-delocalization (permanent). Hyperconjugation (H): σ_C-H to p/π* (permanent, α-H count). Electromeric (E): temporary π-shift. Alkene stability ∝ α-H; HoH ∝ 1 / Alkene Stability.
summary: Master the four electronic displacement effects: Inductive (+I/-I), Resonance (+M/-M), Hyperconjugation, and Electromeric effect.

summaryBox.title: Electronic Hierarchy
summaryBox.takeaway: I-Effect (σ-framework, vanishes after 3-4 C atoms); M-Effect (π/lone pair delocalization across conjugated p-orbitals).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ELECTRONIC DISPLACEMENT ORDERS

+I Effect (Donating):
-O⁻ > -COO⁻ > -C(CH₃)₃ > -CH(CH₃)₂ > -CH₂CH₃ > -CH₃ > -D > -H

-I Effect (Withdrawing):
-NF₃⁺ > -NR₃⁺ > -NH₃⁺ > -NO₂ > -SO₃H > -CN > -CHO > -COOH > -F > -Cl > -Br > -I > -OR > -OH > -C≡CH > -NH₂ > -Ph > -CH=CH₂ > -H

+M / +R Effect (Donating via lone pair):
-O⁻ > -NH₂ > -NHR > -OH > -OR > -NHCOCH₃ > -OCOR > -Ph > -Halogens

-M / -R Effect (Withdrawing via conjugated π):
-NO₂ > -SO₃H > -CN > -CHO > -COR > -COOH > -COOR
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Inductive Effect ($I$)**: Permanent, distance-dependent polarisation of a $\sigma$-bond caused by electronegativity differences along a carbon chain. Vanishes after 3–4 carbons.
• **Resonance / Mesomeric Effect ($M / R$)**: Permanent delocalization of $\pi$-electrons or lone pairs through conjugated continuous $p$-orbital systems.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Hyperconjugation & Heat of Hydrogenation
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Hyperconjugation & Heat of Hydrogenation
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HYPERCONJUGATION & ALKENE STABILITY

• Number of Hyperconjugative Structures = Number of α-Hydrogens (α-H)
• Alkene Stability Order: (CH₃)₂C=C(CH₃)₂ (12αH) > CH₃CH=C(CH₃)₂ (9αH) > (CH₃)₂C=CH₂ (6αH) > CH₃CH=CH₂ (3αH) > CH₂=CH₂ (0αH)
• Heat of Hydrogenation (HoH) ∝ 1 / Alkene Stability ∝ 1 / (Number of α-H)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Hyperconjugation (Nathan-Baker Effect / No-Bond Resonance)**: Delocalization of $\sigma$-electrons of a $\text{C}_\alpha-\text{H}$ bond attached to an $sp^2$-hybridized carbon into an adjacent vacant $p$-orbital (carbocation), half-filled $p$-orbital (radical), or $\pi^*$-antibonding orbital (alkene).
• **Heat of Hydrogenation (HoH)**: Inversely proportional to alkene stability! Highly substituted alkenes have more $\alpha$-hydrogens, higher thermodynamic stability, and release **less heat upon hydrogenation**.

quickRevision: Inductive, Resonance, and Hyperconjugation are permanent effects.
Electromeric effect is a temporary effect occurring only during reagent attack.
Alkene stability increases with the number of α-hydrogens.
Heat of Hydrogenation (HoH) is inversely proportional to alkene stability.
